text:
elaine: quick follow-up to the authn RFC — proposing a claim-minimalization pattern for internal service tokens. idea: keep JWTs tiny (subject, route_id, verb set, exp) and move tenant/project context into a separate signed header envelope. win = smaller tokens, better cache hit rates at gateways, fewer introspection calls.

omar: is this intended for public API keys too or strictly internal svc-to-svc traffic?

elaine: strictly internal initially. public API keys keep current richer claims for compatibility. internal path is where we get the biggest perf gains.

jay: what about endpoints that actually need role lists (eg admin endpoints)? how do we get roles back when needed?

elaine: two patterns: (A) on-demand introspection: gateway/runtime can call authz-introspect for expanded roles (cold path), or (B) ephemeral-expanded tokens: gateway requests a short-lived expanded token from the mint service when route metadata marks it as "needs_expanded_roles". (A) is simpler, (B) avoids an extra authz call but requires mint endpoint and route flags.

mira: audit and tracing implications? if org/project moves to headers we need a way to correlate token->header in logs.

elaine: include a correlation id in both places. header envelope fields: `X-RW-Org`, `X-RW-Project`, `X-RW-Corr-Id` (signed). example minimal token payload (just for clarity):

```
{"sub": "svc:events-worker", "route": "events:write:v1", "verbs": ["create"], "exp": 1720000000}
```

and header: `X-RW-Org: org_999`, `X-RW-Project: proj_7`, `X-RW-Corr-Id: c-xyz789`

omar: caching: be explicit about cache keys. corr id must not be part of the key. propose cache key = (route, subject, token_schema_version).

elaine: agreed. we'll introduce `token_schema_version` in the JWT (schema=2) and use that in cache keys. logs will include corr id for event linking.

jay: security note: moving tenant headers around creates header forgery risk if proxies blindly accept them. gateway must strip any incoming `X-RW-*` headers from external clients and only accept the header envelope from mTLS-authenticated upstreams or signed header blobs verified by KMS.

mira: so requirement: gateway strips inbound headers, internal proxies forward the signed envelope, and gateway verifies signature via KMS/HSM. if not signed or mTLS missing, fail-open? fail-closed?

elaine: fail-closed for tenant assertion. for backwards compat we run dual-validate mode: accept legacy tokens (v1) OR new minimal token + header (v2). in rollout we start with dual mode, migrate services, then disable v1 after a window.

omar: rollout checklist idea: (1) implement header envelope verification and mint/expanded endpoint; (2) mint both v1 and v2 tokens for a transition period; (3) gateway dual-validate; (4) SDK warnings/lints for reading roles off token; (5) route registry flag `requires_expanded_roles` and migration docs.

elaine: we can reuse the existing minting service for expanded tokens — add `/v1/mint/expanded` which issues very short TTL tokens and emits audit events. no new PKI surface.

jay: we should add an SDK lint rule that flags code paths reading `token.roles` and emit a migration hint. also provide a small server-side middleware that materializes roles via introspect so teams can opt-in without changing business logic immediately.

infra-bot: Created ticket RWINF-5555: "claim-minimalization + header-envelope rollout". https://tickets.redwood.example/RWINF-5555

mira: thanks — I'll write a migration playbook and annotate endpoints that will likely need expanded tokens.

elaine: next action: I'll draft the header envelope spec, the mint endpoint contract, and a short gateway dual-validate PR. target to share by EOD Friday.
